audit_findings.title: Post-Thermon financing cost is absent from pre-merger owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $522.531 million increase in gross debt from $214.2 million at 2025 year-end to $736.731 million at June 30, 2026; approximately $32.0 million annual pretax interest at the filed 6.13% weighted-average rate; omitted Thermon OE unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity-level OE method relies on interest expense being included in OE, but the $3.5 million legacy anchor excludes post-merger financing costs while post-close cash and shares enter the bridge and per-share calculation. Thermon operating cash flow is also absent.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to fund any cash portion of the Merger Consideration and related transaction costs with available cash and borrowings under our existing and/or committed credit facilities.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, not merely a possible future risk. The computed incremental interest scale is more than nine times the $3.5 million anchor and could eliminate legacy OE, while adding Thermon's earnings could offset some or all of that reduction. The net direction is therefore mixed, but the valuation conclusion is not supportable on the hybrid perimeter.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild OE on a single post-close perimeter using Thermon operating results, acquisition-debt interest and fee amortization, integration costs, post-close cash, and the final fully diluted share count; rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated cash-flow add-backs may include value belonging to NCI
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.056 million of 2025 net income attributable to NCI, equal to 87.3% of the $3.5 million OE anchor; exact OE overstatement unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable income is combined with consolidated depreciation, working-capital, and capital-expenditure adjustments, potentially including the NCI-owned portion of subsidiary cash flows in OE available to CECO common shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, PPI JV accounted for $ 7.8 million, $ 4.1 million, and $ 4.2 million in net income, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The basis inconsistency is demonstrated if the reported anchor uses parent-attributable income and unallocated consolidated cash-flow adjustments. The exact correction remains unresolved because the ownership allocation of each OE component is not supplied. The filed NCI income is nearly as large as the anchor, so the issue is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Calculate OE entirely on a consolidated basis and deduct the NCI claim, or allocate depreciation, capex, working capital, subsidiary debt service, cash, and distributions by ownership; then rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: A project-timing working-capital outflow may have been capitalized in perpetuity
audit_findings.magnitude: $44.833 million contract-asset outflow plus $16.831 million prepaid-and-other-current-asset outflow in 2025, totaling $61.664 million; normalization adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The one-year working-capital investment reduces the $3.5 million OE anchor and is then embedded in every forecast year and terminal value, even if project billings or collections subsequently reverse the investment.
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease in 2025 was primarily driven by unfavorable changes in net working capital, particularly increased costs on uncompleted contracts and higher prepaid expenses, partially offset by increased customer billings and improved collections on accounts receivable.
audit_findings.explanation: The large 2025 outflows are demonstrated, but their temporary or recurring character is unresolved. The combined filed outflows are 17.6 times the anchor, so even a small reversible portion could materially increase normalized OE and the resulting value. The June 2026 filing does not isolate legacy-project reversals sufficiently to settle the issue after the Thermon acquisition.
audit_findings.action: Trace the 2025 contract assets and prepayments by project into 2026 billings, collections, cancellations, and write-offs; calculate working-capital investment over completed project cycles and rerun using a normalized requirement.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may retain operating earnings from a divested business
audit_findings.magnitude: $107.808 million net sale proceeds and $63.701 million pretax disposal gain; three months of GPS operating and working-capital contribution unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: FY2025 OE may include GPS operations and working-capital movements through March 31 despite forecasting a continuing business without GPS. Sale proceeds may also affect later cash or debt balances and must enter the bridge exactly once.
audit_findings.evidence: On March 31, 2025, the Company finalized the sale of its Global Pump Solutions business to a third party for a purchase price of $ 108.7 million, as adjusted for purchase adjustments.
audit_findings.explanation: The disposal and three-month inclusion are demonstrated, but the record does not quantify GPS's contribution to the $3.5 million anchor. Removing profitable GPS cash flow would lower value, while removing a working-capital-consuming contribution would raise it. The supplied evidence therefore cannot establish direction or materiality, although the mismatch requires resolution.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a GPS carve-out for January through March 2025 covering income, depreciation, capex, working capital, taxes, transaction costs, and retained liabilities; reconcile the $107.808 million proceeds through cash and debt exactly once and rerun if the continuing-business anchor changes.

audit_findings.title: Retained asbestos liabilities may outlast the disposed operations
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.3 million of filed 2025 asbestos litigation expense, equal to 37.1% of the $3.5 million anchor; future uninsured excess unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring settlement and defense cash costs reduce OE, while any liability exceeding recognized expense, reserves, or collectible insurance is a claim ahead of common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: While we divested of the fluid handling business (also known as the Global Pump Solutions business) in the first quarter of 2025, we retained historical asbestos liabilities and the related legacy insurance policies.
audit_findings.explanation: The retained liability and current expense are demonstrated, but current GAAP OE should already include the $1.3 million expense unless it was separately removed. The finding concerns future settlements or failed insurance recoveries not presently established in the numbers, making it a monitoring item rather than a demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the asbestos reserve roll-forward, annual cash settlements and defense costs, claim counts, insurance limits and receivables, and confirmation that no asbestos expense was stripped from OE; rerun if normalized net cash costs exceed the anchor treatment.

audit_findings.title: Balance-sheet control weaknesses directly threaten the OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Errors in contract assets, prepayments, receivables, payables, or billings would change the working-capital adjustment in OE and could also change cash, debt, or other bridge balances.
audit_findings.evidence: We did not consistently assess the proper level of completeness and accuracy of information used in the execution of controls related to balance sheet reconciliations.
audit_findings.explanation: The material weaknesses are demonstrated and remained unremediated at June 30, 2026, but the filings state that they produced no identified material misstatement or revision. That does not demonstrate an error in the $3.5 million anchor. Because the anchor is small and depends heavily on affected balance-sheet movements, an undetected error could matter, but the record cannot quantify or establish its direction.
audit_findings.action: Inspect account-level reconciliation support, audit adjustments, subsequent corrections, remediation testing, and acquired-entity controls for every balance used in OE; recompute and rerun OE for any corrected balances.
